newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Bid bias not over yet.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Bid bias not over yet.

text.p: *Australian semis continue to maintain a bid bias, keeping yield spreads fairly tight to Australian Treasury bonds.
Australian semi-government bonds continue to maintain a bid bias, keeping yield spreads fairly tight to Australian Treasury bonds.

Traders said the positive tone of the semis market since the Reserve Bank included semis stock in commercial bank prime asset ratio (PAR) prudential requirements last month was beginning to show signs of flagging last week.
However, "the bid tone was quickly restored when Moody's raised the credit rating outlook on the states last week," one trader said.
Moody's Investors Service raised the outlook on New South Wales, Victoria, Western Australia and Queensland to improving following similar action on Australia's sovereign foreign currency rating.

The announcements sparked a strong rally in Australian debt market last week, although the market has turned more subdued this week ahead of Thursday's key labour force data which may give some clues to future monetary policy, traders said.

Meanwhile, the Northern Territory Treasury issued A$38 million of promissory notes on Tuesday with December 23 maturity. The unrated notes fetched a yield of 5.25 percent compared with Tuesday's bank bill swap rate of 5.2533 for December 8.
